job.title: Boutique Manager
job.description:
Do you love fashion, and the chance to make a difference? Alexander Appointments is proud to partner with Pink Finss Charity to find a Boutique Manager for Reloved, its curated pre-loved fashion boutique in Sydney’s Hawkesbury District.

Boutique Manager
  • Windsor location | Approx. 30 hours per week | Rostered shifts Monday to Saturday
  • Lead a curated pre-loved fashion boutique with a meaningful local purpose
  • Help support Hawkesbury people and families affected by cancer

Alexander Appointments is proud to partner with Pink Finss Charity to recruit a Boutique Manager for Reloved, its growing pre-loved fashion boutique in the Hawkesbury. Reloved offers quality pre-loved fashion, accessories and premium brands in a welcoming boutique setting. Every sale helps Pink Finss support local people and families affected by cancer. If you love fashion, enjoy leading people and know how to create a store customers want to return to, this is an opportunity to put your retail experience to work for a cause that matters.

The Role
You’ll lead Reloved’s day-to-day operations, creating an exceptional experience for customers while keeping the boutique beautifully presented and commercially focused. Working closely with volunteers and the Warehouse team, you will:
 
  • Lead, train and support volunteers, building an engaged and welcoming team.
  • Deliver excellent customer service and strengthen relationships with the local community.
  • Select, price and merchandise quality pre-loved fashion and accessories, regularly refreshing stock and displays.
  • Monitor sales, identify opportunities to improve performance and support in-store promotions and events.
  • Maintain accurate pricing, tagging and stock processes, and coordinate stock flow with the Warehouse team.
  • Share featured pieces, styling ideas and boutique stories with Pink Finss’ social media provider.
  • Maintain high standards of store presentation, organisation and safety.


About You
You’re a hands-on retail professional with an eye for fashion and the confidence to take ownership of a boutique. You’ll bring:
  • Experience in retail management, boutique fashion or a similar customer-focused role.
  • Strong people skills and the ability to guide and motivate volunteers.
  • A flair for styling and visual merchandising, backed by sound commercial judgement.
  • Excellent customer service, organisation and attention to detail.
  • The initiative to work independently and the ability to collaborate across the charity.
  • A genuine commitment to Pink Finss’ purpose and the Hawkesbury community.

Experience working with volunteers or in a not-for-profit setting is highly regarded, but the right attitude, energy and passion are just as important.

What’s on Offer?
 
  • A part-time role of approximately 30 hours per week, with shifts rostered Monday to Saturday.
  • The chance to shape the next stage of growth for a distinctive, purpose-led boutique.
  • A supportive team of staff and volunteers, with the freedom to bring your ideas and eye for style to the role.
  • The satisfaction of knowing your work helps local people and families affected by cancer.

How to Apply
Please apply by submitting your resume in Word format via the “Apply Now” tab to be considered for this opportunity. Please include a brief cover letter outlining your relevant retail leadership experience and why you would like to join Reloved and Pink Finss Charity.
For a confidential discussion, please contact Alexander Appointments. Only suitable applicants will be contacted.
For other similar roles currently available, please visit our jobs page:
https://www.alexanderappointments.com.au/job-results
We also encourage you to visit our website and create a job alert that will immediately flag you when new opportunities appear:
https://www.alexanderappointments.com.au/job-alerts

Pink Finss Charity is committed to providing an inclusive and welcoming environment. Applications are encouraged from people of all backgrounds and experiences who share a commitment to supporting the local community.

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Operations Manager to join a growing Australian manufacturer at a pivotal stage of its operational transformation.
  
Reporting directly to the COO, you will take ownership of warehouse performance, people, processes and operational capability, while playing a key role in the organisation’s digital transformation and warehouse automation journey.
  
We are looking for an operational leader who can bridge the gap between technology and people - ensuring new systems, automated processes, policies and ways of working are successfully implemented, adopted and embedded across the operation.
  
The Role  
  • Lead warehouse operations, performance and team capability, ensuring the operation continues to deliver against business objectives
  • Drive the warehouse transformation program, including digitisation, system upgrades and robotics/automation initiatives
  • Lead the adoption of new systems, policies, procedures and SOPs, ensuring changes are embedded across the operation
  • Identify opportunities to digitise manual processes, improve workflows and use automation to increase productivity, accuracy and scalability
  • Establish and monitor KPIs, using operational data to identify bottlenecks and drive continuous improvement
  • Partner with the COO and key stakeholders to align technology, processes and people with future business requirements
  • Lead and develop a large operational team through a significant period of change, building accountability, capability and engagement
  • Maintain strong operational standards across inventory, quality, safety, compliance and risk
  
About You
  
You are an experienced Operations Manager, Warehouse Manager, Distribution Manager or similar senior operational leader who has successfully led teams and improved warehouse operations through systems, technology and process transformation.
  
You will bring:  
  • Significant experience leading warehouse, distribution, logistics or manufacturing operations
  • Proven experience delivering digital transformation, system upgrades or warehouse automation projects
  • Strong change-management skills and the ability to bring teams along through significant operational change
  • Experience implementing and embedding new policies, procedures, SOPs and ways of working
  • Strong analytical and KPI-management capability
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing large operational teams
  • Confidence working with ERP, WMS, inventory or other operational technology platforms
  
What's on Offer?  
  • Senior operational leadership role with direct exposure to the COO

  • Be at the forefront of ERP, digitisation and robotics implementation

Reporting to the National Credit Manager, this is a hands-on leadership role responsible for a large team and multiple key functions across master data, collections and payment allocations. You will ideally bring:
